newsitem.title: INDIA: STRONG RUPEE HURTING INDIAN EXPORTS, SAYS MERRILL.
newsitem.headline: STRONG RUPEE HURTING INDIAN EXPORTS, SAYS MERRILL.

text.p: An overvalued rupee is hurting Indian export growth, global investment bank Merrill Lynch said in an India report.
"Exports grew at only four percent in FY1996/97 (April-March), against an 18 percent average growth rate for the previous three years," Merrill's economic monthly said.
"Although we expect export growth to rise in FY98 due to the likely increase in world trade growth, the real appreciation of the rupee is having a negative impact on exports," it said.

"Indian exporters' associations are looking for a seven percent depreciation of the rupee, which is unlikely in our view. Hence we are estimating exports to grow at 12 percent in FY98 compared to our earlier forecast of 20 percent."
The rupee has been steady at about 35.70/80 against the dollar for the past one year.
